title: Autonomous Corrosion‐Self‐Healing Coatings of Microencapsulated Soybean Oil on Mild Steel
content:
A smart self-healing coating based on microencapsulated soybean oil was developed for mild steel protection. The 30 mL SBO formulation exhibited superior healing capability, higher corrosion resistance, and improved coating integrity, as confirmed by SEM, EIS, Tafel polarization, and FTIR analyses.


ABSTRACT

In the oil and gas industry, the failure of protective coatings can cause material degradation, which can be hazardous for safety, asset integrity and environmental health. In this study, the use of an autonomous (self-healing) microencapsulated corrosion coating, using microencapsulated soybean oil (SBO), was explored and the protection was tested for mild steel immersed in 3.5wt.% NaCl solution. The coating formulation consisted of emulsion of soybean oil, EMA, resorcinol, ammonium chloride, 1-octanol, urea, 37wt.% aqueous formaldehyde solution and distilled water. The electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) results showed that the corrosion resistance of the mild steel was greatly improved after being coated with SBO, as compared to the control. The best results have been achieved with the 30 mL SBO coating, with the acceptable impedance response and the lowest corrosion current density. A uniform and protective coating layer that has enhanced corrosion damage resistance has been confirmed by optical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (EDX). The FT-IR data confirmed the inclusion of the soybean oil in the coating and electrochemical tests showed the enhancement of the corrosion protection performance with the concentration of the soybean oil. Based on the results of this study, it appears that the coatings prepared using microencapsulated soybean oil are suitable self-healing corrosion protection systems, which may be more environmentally friendly and sustainable for mild steel.
